Medtronic reported fiscal Q1 2027 on 2026-09-01 am, EPS 1.45 against a 1.39 estimate, a 4.3% beat, with revenue 9.756B against 9.545B, FY27 EPS guidance raised to 5.94-6.00 and organic growth guidance raised to 7.25-7.75%. The 9/1 reaction bar opened 94.00, ran 95.41, flushed to 90.80 and closed 92.04 on 18.8M shares against roughly 6.5M typical - a faded gap that nonetheless HELD 1.53% above the 90.65 pre-print close, which is the exact line SAIC and NTNX failed. The afternoon based 92.24-92.96 for four hours. Today opened 91.47, below yesterday's close and below that base, held above the 90.80 reaction low, and reversed to a 93.39 high. SPECIFIED at 09:45 at a 93.07 limit for 4 shares, CLEAN, no checklist item marked fail, struck AT THE OFFER rather than under the bid as the direct correction to yesterday's DG failure.
entryWatch.trigger: LIVE SPECIFICATION, RE-QUOTED AND CONFIRMED FOR A THIRD HOUR AT 12:21 BY THE MID-SESSION RUN, expiring 15:30 ET today. MDT 93.84 bid / 93.87 ask at 2026-09-02T16:22:13.476932273Z, last 93.850, +1.96% against a 92.04 settled close, on a 0.03 spread that is 0.032% of mark. ALL FOUR NAMED INVALIDATIONS RE-CHECKED AGAINST THE TAPE AND NONE FIRED: the session low is still 91.47, the opening print itself, never traded below on any of thirty-four bars, and the bid is 2.59% clear of it; the 90.80 reaction low is 3.35% below the bid and was never approached; no close exists below 90.65 and the name is 3.19 above it; and MDT at +1.96% cannot close red on a green XLV day from here without a reversal. THE HOUR REVERSES THE DIRECTION OF THE LAST TWO AND IS RECORDED THAT WAY. MDT made a NEW SESSION HIGH OF 94.605 in the 15:25Z bar, minutes after the 11:21 run quoted it at 94.16, and has GIVEN IT BACK: the bid is 0.81% off that high and 0.32 below last hour's reading. So the marketability gap NARROWED for the first time today - 0.86% under the bid at 10:21, 1.16% at 11:21, 0.82% now - after widening in each of the two prior hours. The limit is untouched in both directions. It was never raised while the name ran away from it, and it is not lowered now that the name is walking back toward it; the level was correct and the tape is doing the moving. FILL WINDOW RE-MEASURED: 93.07 was reachable in the 13:45Z strike bar (low 92.510) and the 13:50Z bar (low 92.845) and has NOT been touched since, every bar from 13:55Z having a low of 93.34 or higher - ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY-SEVEN MINUTES untouched against eighty-seven last hour, with the closest approach still the 93.340 low of the 14:35Z bar, 0.29% clear of the limit. The level was correct and immediately fillable for about ten minutes; what is missing is execution. PEER STANDING IS UNCHANGED IN RANK AND WEAKER IN SUBSTANCE: MDT still trails ABT +2.78% and BSX +2.79% and still leads BDX +1.56%, ZBH +1.81%, XLV +0.70% and SPY +0.46%, so the three-of-five reading from 11:21 stands - but MDT gave back 0.34 points this hour while BSX ADDED 0.29, making MDT the weakest of the three leaders hour-over-hour and widening the gap behind the leaders from 0.20 to 0.83 points. The alpha ratios survive at 4.3x SPY and 2.8x XLV only because the benchmarks faded alongside it, which is a smaller claim off a smaller absolute move and is written down as the smaller claim.
entryWatch.why: The primary case is the day-2 structure off a beat AND raise, not the cohort. That ordering is deliberate: yesterday's DG entry rested on a cohort-laggard framing that inverted by 14:22 while the spec sat unfilled, so the sympathy-laggard reading is available here but is written down as a secondary tailwind rather than the load-bearing claim. Also recorded before the outcome: eight price-target raises landed in one pre-market (Mizuho 100-115, Leerink 104-111, Evercore 105-106, Wells Fargo 102-104, Baird 91-100, Truist 86-99, Stifel 80-95, Jefferies 88-95) with a mean target of 101.74 - which sits BELOW the mechanical +20% take-profit at 111.68. This trade most likely closes on the time stop rather than the target, and it says so at entry rather than discovering it at the retro.

entryWatch.trigger: NOT RE-STRUCK, AND THE REFUSAL IS RE-AFFIRMED FOR A FOURTH TIME TODAY. Quoted at 09:45 at 131.94 bid / 132.37 ask, leaving the dead 128.40 limit 2.68% below the market; not re-quoted this hour because nothing this slot could learn about DG would make re-striking it permissible, and a row this run did not re-pull does not get this run's clock. The 2026-08-18 rule is explicit that widening the time was never permission to widen the price. What changed this hour is the companion case rather than this one: MDT stopped running and came BACK toward its limit, which is precisely the outcome the identical refusal is waiting for on both names. The board held the line on two names in one session, and on one of them the tape has started to reward the patience rather than punish it - recorded here because this row would otherwise only ever be updated on the hours when the refusal looked expensive.
entryWatch.why: Kept as the standing example. The spec died VALID rather than wrong - none of its three invalidations fired - and it still did not fill, because it was struck 0.38% under the bid of a name that rose on every bar. Today's MDT entry is struck AT the offer for that reason, and this row is what that decision is answering.

entryWatch.trigger: STILL REFUSED, AND STILL BREAKING DOWN. SAIC is 123.11 bid / 124.39 ask at 2026-09-02T13:41:55.491665676Z, last 123.50, -2.90% against a 126.78 settled close, on a 1.03% spread. entryWatch.why: This is the row MDT is graded against. Same shape at the start - a large beat, a gap, a fade - and opposite resolutions: SAIC lost its pre-print close on day 2 and MDT held 1.53% above it. The rulebook has no rule that says 'a big beat is a buy'; it has a rule about what the tape does with the gap, and these two names are the worked example of why.
